mercado: One of Europe's largest covered markets, in a Modernista building of iron, glass and ceramics: stalls of fruit and vegetables, fish, jamón, cheese, paella rice and Valencia oranges. Outside is Plaza del Mercado.
lonja: The 15th-century silk exchange, a UNESCO site: the great trading hall with spiral columns rising like palm trees, the courtyard of orange trees and the tower. From outside it's one of Europe's finest Gothic civic buildings.
seu: Cathedral, Miguelete and Plaza de la Virgen

The Gothic, Baroque and neoclassical cathedral, with the chapel that keeps the Santo Cáliz, the chalice that tradition says is the Holy Grail. Next to it is the Miguelete (or Micalet), the octagonal bell tower with a view over the whole city. Plaza de la Virgen in front has the Turia fountain and the Basilica of the Desamparados.
carmen: Barrio del Carmen and Torres de Serranos

The oldest quarter, with narrow lanes, murals, churches and little squares, closed to the north by the Torres de Serranos, the medieval gate in the walls. From the top you see the dry riverbed turned into a garden. To the west, the other gate, the Torres de Quart, still bears cannonball marks.
cac: Santiago Calatrava's futuristic complex of white and water: the eye-shaped Hemisfèric, the Palau de les Arts, the Umbracle and the Science Museum. One of the most photographed places in the city, especially in the morning or at sunset with the reflections in the pools.
turia: The bed of the old River Turia, diverted after the 1957 flood, is now a nine-kilometre park through the city, with trees, sports fields, historic bridges and the Palau de la Música. Walk or cycle all the way to the City of Arts and Sciences.
bellas: Museum of Fine Arts (Museo de Bellas Artes)

One of Spain's most important painting museums, in the former college of San Pío V: Valencian Gothic panels, Velázquez, Goya and the great canvases of Sorolla, the painter of Valencia's light. It's next to the Viveros garden.
colon: Mercado de Colón, Estación del Norte and the bullring

The Mercado de Colón is a Modernista brick-and-ceramic building now full of cafés and bars; a little further on are the Estación del Norte, decorated with oranges, and the bullring. Valencia's Eixample has elegant early-20th-century buildings.
ruzafa: The liveliest and least touristy neighbourhood, with streets full of murals, local cafés, shops and small restaurants. The Ruzafa market, on Plaza Baró de Cortes, is the heart of the area.
ocean: Europe's largest aquarium, divided into the world's habitats: the Mediterranean, the Red Sea, the Arctic, Antarctica, tropical oceans. There are sharks, belugas, walruses and an underwater tunnel. A full visit takes half a day.
malvarrosa: Malvarrosa Beach and the Paseo Marítimo

Valencia's city beach: wide sand, a seafront promenade with terraces and paella restaurants. The neighbouring Cabanyal district has fishermen's houses with tiled façades and bars frequented by locals.
